newsitem.title: GERMANY: DTB Bunds to regain strength after corrective dip.
newsitem.headline: DTB Bunds to regain strength after corrective dip.

text.p: German Bunds started Friday's session in positive ground, reversing some of the losses sustained on Thursday when the Sepetmber futures contract was overpowered by resistance.
Analysts said that once the DTB September future failed to fight its way through an upside barrier at 102.92/3 on Thursday, some players became nervous and moved in to take profits from recent gains.
But the dip down should now provide the market with more fuel, they said, tempting buyers into the market at lower levels.
By 0631 GMT, the September future was trading 10 basis points higher at 102.81, having already reached up to a high of 102.85 in early business.

"(Yesterday's move was) merely a test to wash out some of the longs, but the sustainability of some of the long-position holders has been somewhat impressive," said Dirk Auderheide, analyst at DMG Futures and Options in Frankfurt.

He said the correction, which based at 102.53 and had already turned up again in late trade on Thursday, should lend the market new bullish momentum and said any weakness towards the 102.60/65 area should be seen as a buying opprtunity.

Analysts said the May retail sales and June cost of living data did little to ruffle the market, merely confirming the long-held view that the economic recovery remains slow and inflation dangers are slight.
Data released just before the market opened showed retail sales declined a real 2.3 percent in May versus a year earlier, while pan-German CPI inflation was up 1.7 year-on-year in June.
"All in all, these data will attract less market attention than the U.S. PPI (producer price) figures due in the afternoon," MMS analysts said in a research note.
The U.S. numbers are due at 1230 GMT.
Analysts polled by Reuters expect producer prices to be unchanged on the month in June, but up 0.1 percent on the year.
In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark Bund was quoted at 103.25 at 0654 GMT, offering a bid yield of 5.558 percent.

The yield spread to Treasuries reflected the underperformance of the German market in late trade on Thursday, having slimmed to 79 basis points from around 81 basis points at the end of Wednesday's session.
